name: Alex Lee
title: California State Assemblymember, Chair of the Assembly Human Services Committee
district: California State Assembly District 24 (parts of Santa Clara and Alameda Counties, including San Jose, Milpitas, Fremont, Newark, and Sunol; represented District 25 from 2020 to 2022 before redistricting)
years_of_service: December 7, 2020 to present. Lee was re-elected in 2022 and 2024, and advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary as the incumbent candidate for the November 3, 2026 general election.
background: Lee was born in San Jose, California, on July 11, 1995, and grew up in Milpitas, graduating from Milpitas High School. He earned a B.A. in political science and communications from the University of California, Davis in 2017, where he served as student body president. Before running for office he interned for California legislators including then-Assemblymember Mike Honda and Assemblymember Evan Low, and worked as a full-time legislative policy aide to State Senator Henry Stern focusing on public safety, climate change, and education. (Sources: official Assembly biography, a24.asmdc.org/biography; Wikipedia, Alex Lee (Ballotpedia corroborates UC Davis 2017 and legislative-aide background).)

Lee was first elected in November 2020 to the open Assembly District 25 seat, defeating Republican Bob Brunton 70.5% to 29.5%; he had placed second in a crowded nine-candidate primary. Following 2021 redistricting his district was renumbered District 24. He was re-elected in 2022 (69.1% to 30.9% over Brunton), in 2024 (66.1% to 33.9% over Brunton), and advanced from the June 2026 primary with 62.1% of the vote against Republican Max Hsia. At 25 years old when he took office, Lee became the youngest Asian American legislator ever elected in California and the first openly bisexual member of the California Legislature. He chairs the California Legislative Progressive Caucus and identifies as a democratic socialist; he has been endorsed by the Democratic Socialists of America. (Sources: Ballotpedia, Alex Lee; Wikipedia, Alex Lee.)

In the Legislature, Lee has focused on housing policy, including "social housing" (publicly developed, mixed-income housing) proposals, and on campaign-finance reform, wealth taxation, and consumer/tenant protections. He chairs the Assembly Human Services Committee and, in the 2025 to 2026 session, also chaired a Select Committee on Social Housing. He was named "Legislator of the Year" by the Golden State Manufactured-Home Owners League and by California Attorneys for Criminal Justice in his first year in office, and by the East Bay Young Democrats in 2022. (Sources: official Assembly biography; Wikipedia, Alex Lee.)

voting_record_highlights: SB 42 (2025 to 2026), the California Fair Elections Act of 2026: Lee was one of seven principal coauthors of the bill in its final form (alongside Becker, Berman, Blakespear, Kalra, Pellerin, and Stern), with Umberg, Allen, and Cervantes as lead authors. The Senate concurred in Assembly amendments 29 to 8 on September 13, 2025, and Gov. Gavin Newsom signed it October 2, 2025 as Chapter 245, Statutes of 2025, placing the measure before voters as Proposition 4 on the November 2026 ballot. Full detail on the measure itself is covered elsewhere and not duplicated here. (Source: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov bill status for SB 42.)

AB 259 (2023 to 2024), a wealth tax on Californians' net worth above $1 billion (later $50 million), paired with False Claims Act enforcement provisions: Lee was the lead author, with Ash Kalra as principal coauthor. The bill did not receive a floor vote before the constitutional two-year deadline and "died pursuant to Art. IV, Sec. 10(c) of the Constitution" on January 31, 2024. (Source: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov bill status for AB 259.)

AB 309 (2023 to 2024), the Social Housing Act, which would have created a state Social Housing Program to develop mixed-income housing on surplus public land: Lee was a lead author with Wendy Carrillo and Ash Kalra. It passed the Senate concurrence vote 56 to 16 on September 14, 2023, but Gov. Newsom vetoed it on October 7, 2023, citing cost and state-property concerns. (Source: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov bill status for AB 309.)

AB 1729 (2025 to 2026), which would have required state agencies to publicly report telework participation and office-space utilization data: Lee was the lead author. It passed the Senate 31 to 6 on August 27, 2026, but Gov. Newsom vetoed it on September 18, 2026. (Source: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov bill status for AB 1729.)

AB 2465 (2025 to 2026), eliminating certain state tax benefits for private contractors operating immigration detention facilities: Lee was a lead author with Liz Ortega. It passed the Senate concurrence vote 58 to 19 on August 26, 2026 and was enrolled and presented to the Governor on September 3, 2026; as of this profile's retrieval date (September 22, 2026) the Governor's decision had not yet been recorded in the bill's official status history. (Source: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov bill status for AB 2465.)
attendance: No individually published floor-attendance or voting-participation record for Assemblymember Lee was found. The California State Assembly does not publish a per-member attendance scorecard; the only public records are bill-by-bill roll-call votes at leginfo.legislature.ca.gov, which is what the voting-record entries above are drawn from. A CalMatters Digital Democracy legislator profile exists for other members with bill-passage and interest-group vote-alignment statistics, but a working profile page for Lee could not be located during this research (the expected URL returned a 404).
